reports.description:
My PC, Windows 7 Ultimate SP1 64bits, was hacked on 10 May 22 by bitlockerlock.unlock@gmail.com or davidblaine@mail2world.com. I tend to leave it on all the time and I was surprised to log into it and find that all my files (>600GB) had been moved to my secondary drive (no OS). 
The only thing on my desktop was a text file explaining the situation and demanding a ransom in Bitcoins._x000D_
The drive was encrypted with Microsofts BitLocker technology, something Ive only heard of, never set up (my 1st mistake)._x000D_
I contacted the hacker via email to make sure I received the password. He confirmed it and just insisted that he make the transfer soon._x000D_
As I dont have cryptocurrency skills, it took me 1 day to open the account and deposit the amount. He asked me BRL 700 (~US$137). My exchange would only allow transferring the amount 3 days later, for security reasons._x000D_
During that time I researched many things. Other attacks by the same hacker, brute force attack programs, bitcracker, passware, etc..._x000D_
Ill tell you right now, none of them will work._x000D_
The passware costs more than $800, which is unfeasible depending on the situation._x000D_
Bitcracker, despite being a noble initiative, requires high-performance NVIDIA graphics cards to try to crack the password._x000D_
Warning: Do not format your encrypted drive, you will lose everything, no return. Dont waste your time trying to guess the password. It uses long passwords and with non-ASCII characters, it is impossible to guess. Theres no human way to get his data back if he doesnt send the password. (And thats not his disclosure, its a fact!)_x000D_
In my case, the amount was doable and I chose to pay, contrary to the recommendation of several security sites._x000D_
